A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S-VBMC research. All 24 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original posterior-approximation experiments on two synthetic and two neuroscience problems, including numerical results, posterior visualizations, and computational timings.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and additional stacking comparisons, bias-correction experiments, runtime measurements, and convergence-filtering outcomes.

M1.justification: The original component-weight optimization remains, but Section 5.2 introduces a substantive output correction: capping the estimated expected log-joint using either run-level or component-level medians. Appendix A.3.1 also introduces a variant optimizing only whole-posterior weights. The expanded softmax and Jacobian descriptions document implementation; they do not independently establish changes to the original algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the 2D clustered GMM, 2D narrow ring, five-parameter neuronal model, and six-parameter multisensory model using participant S1. The noiseless and Gaussian-noise scenarios remain the same. New analyses reuse these problems; revised neuronal-data attribution does not establish different task or population coverage.

E2.justification: v3 retains single-run VBMC and BBVI with 50 or 500 mixture components, while adding uniform Naive Stacking throughout the main comparisons and optimized posterior-only stacking in Appendix A.3.1. Tables A.3–A.4 confirm their participation. These controls substantially strengthen comparisons against simpler ways of combining the same VBMC outputs.

E3.justification: v3 reports an additional eligibility requirement, maximum component variance below 5, beyond v1's convergence requirement, and selects the first 100 eligible runs. Added analyses use true-log-joint Monte Carlo checks and define total parallel runtime as the slowest of 40 VBMC runs plus stacking. The main likelihood budgets, noise settings, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing whether weight optimization improves on averaging and whether component-level optimization improves on posterior-level optimization. Figures 6–7 diagnose expected-log-joint bias and compare two capping heuristics against Monte Carlo estimates. Appendices A.3.2 and A.4.1 add total-runtime and convergence-failure analyses. v1's run-count curves, noise comparisons, and posterior examples were already present.

E5.justification: The reported stacking repetitions increase from ten to twenty per stack size. Medians with interquartile ranges are replaced throughout by medians with 95% confidence intervals computed using 10,000 bootstrap resamples. Both versions use 100 retained VBMC runs; v3's newly disclosed attempted and excluded run counts do not establish how many attempts v1 required.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for Naive Stacking, posterior-only optimization, debiasing, total runtime, and filtering, while revising existing VBMC/S-VBMC estimates. For example, noiseless-ring S-VBMC with ten runs reports median delta-LML of 0.15 in v1 Table A.1 and 0.034 in v3 Table A.3. Changed selection and repetition protocols preclude treating this as an isolated algorithmic gain. Figure 7 newly shows capping containing bias growth.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a substantive mathematical treatment of run-specific coordinate transformations, deriving consistent stacked densities, entropy calculations, and expected-log-joint corrections. Section 5.2 formally defines the capped estimators. The identical-posterior example explaining selection-induced bias already appeared in v1 Appendix A.8 and is retained in v3 Section 5.1; it is not a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central claims of parallel, evaluation-free posterior stacking and improved posterior approximation remain. v3 adds inexpensive ELBO-bias mitigation as a contribution in its outline and conclusion, replacing v1's deferral of debiasing to future work. Its introduction also explicitly limits the intended operating regime to approximately ten dimensions or fewer.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and limitations: inherited GP dimensional scaling, when ordinary MCMC is preferable, incomplete neuronal-posterior accuracy, and dependence of runtime advantages on likelihood cost. It explains that capping leaves residual bias and does not remove the bias-producing optimization mechanism. These qualifications and practical interpretations go well beyond v1's brief bias warning and overhead discussion.

D1.justification: v3 supplies Algorithm 1, weight initialization and softmax details, coordinate-transformation handling, entropy sample counts of 20 during optimization and 100 afterward, Adam learning rate 0.1, and processor/RAM specifications. It also reports filtering counts, provides an S-VBMC Python-package link, and revises neuronal model/data attribution. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures, without proving corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: The brief related-work paragraph becomes a substantially expanded positioning discussion. v3 adds historical stacking references such as Wolpert (1992) and Yao et al. (2018), additional divide-and-conquer and federated inference literature, and an explicit contrast with direct Bayesian-quadrature approaches including Osborne, Gunter, and Adachi. Existing distinctions from variational boosting and parallel MCMC are retained and developed.

P1.justification: v3 extensively reorganizes and expands the narrative. Background, algorithm, and experiments receive dedicated subsections; related work, model descriptions, metrics, BBVI details, overhead, and bias material move from appendices into the main exposition. A substantial discussion section and reorganized technical appendices replace the earlier compact structure, alongside extensive explanatory rewriting.

P2.justification: The synthetic-results figure is redesigned from two rows overlaying noise conditions into four separate condition rows with additional comparator displays. v1's synthetic posterior illustration and overhead figure move into the main text as v3 Figures 2 and 5. New bias and ablation figures, runtime/filtering tables, expanded comparison-table rows, revised captions, and a different document layout substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 left ELBO debiasing unresolved and lacked controls separating optimized stacking from simple aggregation. v3 addresses these important gaps with Naive Stacking and posterior-only comparisons, direct Monte Carlo bias checks, and an empirically evaluated correction. Detailed algorithm and transformation documentation, filtering transparency, and clearer applicability limits substantially improve reproducibility and interpretability. The correction remains heuristic and leaves residual bias, but those acknowledged limits do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and technical completeness.
